pilot.summary: Three-player pod at Tom Beloy's — Alex on mono-red Tannuk, Tom on Merfolk. Alex resolved Blood Moon on turn two or three and every nonbasic became a Mountain, so Smothering Tithe and everything multicoloured were uncastable and I was down to the all-red dragons. I got there with Moltensteel Dragon at the end, paying sixteen life to pump it and hitting Alex for twelve. I am not building around Blood Moon; the lesson I took was to have the mana base audited holistically.

Five-player pod at Oliver's, seat 4, and the first game on the new land base after raising it 31 to 36 that same day. It did not help — mulliganed once, sat on four or five lands on turns six and seven while Alex was tapping for twelve on turns four and five, and the cost reducer got removed so the discount engine never did its job. After that it was repeated wipes: board established, board erased. I won by staying off the radar and closing at the end, and my own read is that the deck did not win, the table's attrition did.

Game 2 of three at Oliver's, five-player pod, and the first validation game for the refactor. The mana worked — turn-one land into Sol Ring and Arcane Signet, turn-two Bloom Tender — and I curved into Miirym, Gadrak and Terror of the Peaks. Then I played Gadrak a turn too early and telegraphed the whole thing: the table read "Sean is swinging for 28 in the air" and converged, Tom killing all three artifacts so Gadrak could not activate, Alex fighting the dragons with his fight deck, Ryan removing more. Loss, and the lesson written down was speed without protection or politics makes me the obvious kill target before I can close.

Four-player pod at my house — Stuart on an Animar precon, Steven on CC Weather, David on Squirrels. I sacked a land to tutor, found Terror of the Peaks, and after that every dragon ETB was about ten targeted damage across three targets, which I used as spot removal to take out two commanders. Then I telegraphed again: the treasure pile plus fireballing every ETB made me the obvious problem, David called it out, and three players picked me apart inside one rotation. Steven flew under the radar with his tap/untap engine and won it — a political loss, not a deck loss.

Five-player pod at Oliver's; I arrived late, missed game one, and Oliver won every game that night. I was going to play Heliod and swapped to Ur-Dragon because the table said "creatures". No green source all game, so Farseek and the green dragons sat in hand, and Enlightened Tutor went for Sol Ring when it should have found a green rock or a signet. Firespitter Whelp with Twinflame Tyrant and Panharmonicon was pinging and doubling, but I cast Twinflame before the big dragons were down and it was removed immediately — the same too-early pattern, no treasure engine online at any point, and no counterspells left to answer any of it.

Three-player at my house — Stephen on Sisay, Weatherlight Captain, which is getting bonkers now that he sequences it right, and Stuart on a new Rot-Cleaver zombie deck with decayed chump blockers. I kept three lands, Arcane Signet, Smaug the Magnificent and Thrakkus the Butcher, never found the land to cast either dragon on time, and I do not stand by the keep. When The Ur-Dragon landed and Stephen targeted it, Bloom Tender was untapped with all five colours out — five mana, not two or three — and Return of the Wildspeaker was in hand for ten cards off the dragon; I did not pause, did not tap Tender, and let the removal resolve. Stephen killed Stuart through everything and had me at five, then swung with everything and left himself open at five with no blockers, so I untapped, swung with the dorks plus the two Spirit tokens Forbidden Orchard had given me, and squeaked out the win by not being too loud.

Second game of the night at Oliver's, four-player pod with Oliver, Ryan and Alex, Tom away in India, played on the latest pinned list. Faeburrow Elder came down early, then Urza's Incubator, and two discounts plus tapping the Elder put The Ur-Dragon on the battlefield on turn five. It has no haste, so I swung with the dragon I already had, drew a card off the trigger and put Miirym from hand onto the battlefield; with five colours online I was tapping for ten mana on turn six, and I politicked Ryan into leaving the Ur-Dragon alone even as Alex and Oliver told him he was being stupid. Next turn Firespitter Whelp under Panharmonicon, with Miirym copying the Whelp, was by my count six then twelve damage on every dragon cast: Alex died fast, a couple of spells drained the rest, and I won on turn six or seven behind a board of 4/4 flying dragons. The best game of Magic I think I have ever played, and my instruction afterward is to leave this deck alone.

read.what_it_does: It ramps into a nine-drop on turn five and then charges the table for every dragon that arrives. On the current list that is one game and it did exactly that: Faeburrow Elder early, Urza's Incubator, two discounts plus the Elder for seven mana, The Ur-Dragon on turn five, its attack trigger putting Miirym onto the battlefield, ten mana on turn six, and the next turn Firespitter Whelp under Panharmonicon with Miirym copying the Whelp — by your count six then twelve damage on every dragon cast — killing Alex first and draining the rest for a win on turn six or seven (007). That is the manual's arrival-priced plan showing up at a table, and it is the first logged game where the dragons closed rather than the table's attrition: the two earlier wins were last seat standing after four players ground each other down (002, on V2) and a swing with the dorks into Stephen after he left himself open at five (006, on V4). One game is not a rate, and you said so yourself: if it could do that consistently it would be a tier four, and it is a three, optimized (007).
read.how_it_plays: Fast and loud. The mana has worked since the dork-and-rock density went in on V3 — turn-one Sol Ring and Arcane Signet, turn-two Bloom Tender (003) — and on the current list the Elder plus two discounts is a nine-drop on turn five, "exactly the mana ramp we built" (007). The board is legible from across the table, and the pod reads lethal before it is presented: Tom killing all three artifacts so Gadrak could not activate while Alex fought the dragons and Ryan removed more (003, on V3); three players picking you apart inside one rotation after the treasure pile and a fireball on every ETB (004, on V4). In 007 the table read it the same way — Alex and Oliver told Ryan he was being stupid — but Ryan was the seat with the removal and you talked him out of using it; your guess is he let the Ur-Dragon stay because he doubts your ability to close. Every table it sits at runs heavy removal: creature removal and wipes at Oliver's (002, on V2; 003), counters and targeted removal from Stephen and wipes from Stuart at home (006, on V4). Where it ends up: dead to a converged table (003, 004), stuck behind a missing colour or a land that never came (005, 006), quiet and last seat standing (002, 006), or — once, on this list — steamrolling from turn five with nobody able to deal with a board of 4/4 flyers (007).
mindful_of: The order that worked in 007 is the one you wrote down after 005: dragons first, the doubler after. The Ur-Dragon on turn five and Miirym on turn six, then Firespitter Whelp and Panharmonicon the turn after with something for them to multiply (007). The loss it answers was Twinflame Tyrant cast before the big dragons were down and removed immediately (005, on V4), and the cause you named was that you do not like having unspent mana.

Politics decides whether the loud line lives. It is the recorded cause of two losses — Gadrak a turn early and the table read 28 in the air (003, on V3); the treasure pile plus fireballing every ETB, David called it out (004, on V4) — and it is what carried 007: you politicked Ryan into not removing the Ur-Dragon and not killing you, against Alex and Oliver telling him not to. The lesson from 004 still stands beside it: call out the quiet assembler before he is unanswerable — Steven's tap/untap engine won that game while the table was busy with you.

A five-colour dork is five mana once all five colours are out, not two or three. Bloom Tender was untapped with the commander on the table and you read it low (006, on V4); in 007 Faeburrow Elder, basically a Bloom Tender, was the ramp — tapping it for a bunch of mana got you to seven, and with five colours online and the Ur-Dragon out it was ten mana on turn six.

Pause before resolution. When removal is coming in or the commander is under threat, stop and scan instant-speed responses, dorks that can tap, and cards in hand before the stack closes (006, on V4). The card you failed to cast that game, Return of the Wildspeaker, left the list on V6, so the card-level half of that lesson is about a list this deck no longer runs; the rule itself is not, and V6 added the instant-speed cards the rule is for — none of which 007 names, because nobody pointed removal at the dragon.

Two keeps you do not stand by, both on V4, both on cards still in the 99. No green source all game in 005, with Farseek and the green-needing dragons stranded in hand even though Delighted Halfling, Birds of Paradise and Bloom Tender are all in there — your rule: no green source, consider shipping it. Three lands, Arcane Signet, Smaug and Thrakkus in 006, and the land to cast either never came — that was a hand to ship.
Tutors get spent on speed instead of on the problem in front of you — Enlightened Tutor found Sol Ring when the game was a fixing game (005, on V4).

The pod at Oliver's runs heavy creature removal and board wipes, and on V2 this deck made nothing on the way down: board established, board erased, repeat (002). 003 is the same table taking the board apart on V3. 007 is the same four seats minus Tom, and the removal was there — Ryan had it and chose not to use it. The loud line has now won at that table exactly once, and it won because one seat decided not to answer it.
No treasure engine online at any point in 005, on a list whose treasure pile was the story of 004 (both V4). 007 does not mention treasure at all; the mana came from the Elder and the discounts.
Deck choice can be its own problem. You swapped off Heliod to Ur-Dragon because the table said "creatures" (005), and your own view — Oliver disagrees — is that mismatched decks make salt.
Temperament. You wanted to scoop in 005, took a breath and played it out. The rule you set is to stay on the field and get even inside the game.
read.what_changed: Two versions since the last read, one game on them, and your instruction after that game is: leave this deck alone (007). V5 was the scan of the sleeved list on 2026-09-17 — the drift was five cards — and Forbidden Orchard went out with it, so the two Spirit tokens that closed 006 came from a land this deck no longer runs. V6 on 2026-09-20 merged final-v2, the protection package — Stubborn Denial, Mithril Coat, Asceticism, Steel Hellkite, Transcendent Dragon, Whirlwing Stormbrood — with Hellkite Courser kept and a Forest becoming a Mountain; Return of the Wildspeaker, Rishkar's Expertise, Radiant Destiny, Sarkhan Fireblood, Utvara Hellkite and Worldly Tutor left. That package is the answer to the gap named in two notes — "I cut protection and counters for speed, and it showed" (003, on V3), "I now have zero responses" (005, on V4) — and 007 did not test it: the note names none of the six, the dragon stayed because Ryan was talked out of removing it, and the game was over before the table got a second look. So whether V6 fixed the converge is still open; what 007 shows is that the ramp half the earlier versions built — V2's five lands after the Blood Moon game (001), V3's dorks and rocks (003) — now puts a nine-drop on the battlefield on turn five on the list as it stands. The card-level lessons from 001 (Smothering Tithe, Moltensteel Dragon) and 006 (Return of the Wildspeaker, Forbidden Orchard) are superseded; they were true of lists this deck no longer runs. Everything else the older games taught rests on cards still in the 99.
